name: Through the Forest Gate
oracle_text: Look at the top twenty cards of your library, put any number of land cards from among them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle. You gain 8 life.
blocked_sentences: Look at the top twenty cards of your library, put any number of land cards from among them onto the battlefield tapped, then shuffle.

needs.what: an effect that bounds a pool to the top N cards of a library and then lets the chooser take any number of the cards in that pool that match a selector to a named destination, leaving the rest where they were. Wanted here as something like {"op": "look_at_top", "amount": {"const": 20}, "selector": {"types": ["Land"]}, "count": "any", "destination": "battlefield", "tapped": true, "shuffle": true}. The free-subset decision this needs already exists -- `scry` and `surveil` both call `ask_objects(..., 0, len(top), ...)` over `library[:amount]` -- so the missing piece is a top-N pool whose destination is not fixed to the bottom of the library or the graveyard.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `search_library` is the only op that moves library cards to the battlefield tapped, and it builds its pool from the *entire* library (`for oid in ctx.state.players[pid].library`), with no amount/depth clause. Written with it, this card would be an unconditional tutor for every land in a 40+ card deck rather than a look at twenty, which is a strictly stronger card and not the printed line -- the difference is exactly what makes the card a gamble. The three ops that do read `library[:amount]` -- `scry`, `surveil`, `two_piles` -- each hard-wire where the looked-at cards may go (bottom of library, graveyard, hand-or-graveyard); none accepts a destination or a selector, so none can put lands onto the battlefield tapped. The selector language cannot close the gap either: `resolve_pool` maps `zone: "library"` to the whole `zone_list(Zone.LIBRARY)`, and `SELECTOR_KEYS` has no depth/top-of-library key, so `put_onto_battlefield` over a library selector would also see every card in the deck. Also note `count` in a selector is "all" or a fixed number, so the printed "any number" needs the free-subset spelling tracked under `any_number_of` unless this op bakes it in the way `scry` and `surveil` do.
